title: Whole Numbers to 6 Digits: Place Value, Comparing and Ordering
seo_title: Grade 5 Whole Numbers to 6 Digits Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Count forwards and backwards in whole number intervals up to at least 10 000; order, compare and represent numbers to at least 6-digit numbers; recognise the place value of digits in whole numbers to at least 6-digit numbers.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 5 whole numbers worksheets: 6-digit place value, reading and writing numbers, expanded notation, counting and comparing. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Hundred thousands, ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens, units.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A 6-digit number has hundred thousands, ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens and units: 245 306.
  • In 245 306 the 4 is worth 40 000, and the 0 shows that there are no tens.
  • Expanded notation: 245 306 = 200 000 + 40 000 + 5 000 + 300 + 6.
  • To compare, start from the biggest place.

Examples

Example

Three hundred and eight thousand and fifty

308 thousands

0 hundreds, 5 tens, 0 units

Answer: 308 050

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Value or digit?The digit 4 in 245 306 has a value of 40 000.
A missing 0Write 0 for an empty place.
Last digits firstCompare from the left.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 5 say about whole numbers?
faq.a: Order, compare and represent numbers to at least 6-digit numbers, recognise the place value of digits in whole numbers to at least 6 digits, and count forwards and backwards in whole number intervals up to at least 10 000.

faq.q: How do South Africans write big numbers?
faq.a: With a space between groups of three digits: 245 306.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 7 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 7 thousands = 7 000. The digit is 7, but its value is 7 000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 7 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 7 ten thousands = 70 000. The digit is 7, but its value is 70 000.

items.q: In 834 691, which digit is in the ten thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. In 834 691 the ten thousands digit is 3, worth 30 000.

items.q: In 203 684, which digit is in the hundred thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. In 203 684 the hundred thousands digit is 2, worth 200 000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 4 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 4 ten thousands = 40 000. The digit is 4, but its value is 40 000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 5 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 5 hundreds = 500. The digit is 5, but its value is 500.

items.q: Which number has a 7 in the ten thousands place?
items.e: In a 6-digit number the ten thousands place is the 2nd digit from the left (5th from the right). In 376 859 the 7 is there, so it is worth 70 000.
Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place: 500 000 + 3 000 + 80 + 2 = 503 082.

items.q: What number is 60 000 + 700 + 4?
items.e: Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place: 60 000 + 700 + 4 = 60 704.

items.q: Which number is three hundred and four thousand and twenty?
items.e: Write the thousands part first: three hundred and four thousand → 304. Then the last three digits: twenty → 020. Fill every empty place with 0: 304 020.

items.q: Which number is seventy thousand, six hundred and five?
items.e: Write the thousands part first: seventy thousand → 70. Then the last three digits: six hundred and five → 605. Fill every empty place with 0: 70 605.

items.q: Which number is two hundred and fifty thousand and nine?
items.e: Write the thousands part first: two hundred and fifty thousand → 250. Then the last three digits: nine → 009. Fill every empty place with 0: 250 009.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 7 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 7 ten thousands = 70 000. The digit is 7, but its value is 70 000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 6 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 6 hundreds = 600. The digit is 6, but its value is 600.

items.q: Which number has a 6 in the hundred thousands place?
items.e: 632 054 has 6 hundred thousands, 3 ten thousands, 2 thousands, 0 hundreds, 5 tens, 4 ones. The hundred thousands digit is 6.

items.q: Which number has 0 ten thousands?
items.e: 708 516 is 7 hundred thousands, 0 ten thousands, 8 thousands, 5 hundreds, 1 ten and 6 ones. The other numbers have 8 or 7 ten thousands.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 8 is in the tens place, so it is worth 8 tens = 80. The digit is 8, but its value is 80.

items.q: Which number has a 4 in the thousands place?
items.e: 274 019 has 2 hundred thousands, 7 ten thousands, 4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 1 ten, 9 ones. The thousands digit is 4.

items.q: 478 300 = ☐ thousands and 3 hundreds. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 478 300 = 478 000 + 300. 478 000 is 478 thousands. So 478 300 = 478 thousands and 3 hundreds. (8 is only the thousands digit.)

items.q: In 903 407, which digit is in the tens place?
items.e: 903 407 is 9 hundred thousands, 0 ten thousands, 3 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones. The tens digit is 0: there are no tens.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. In 635 274 the red 6 is in the hundred thousands place.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. In 428 916 the red 2 is in the ten thousands place.

items.q: In 743 816, which digit is in the ten thousands place?
items.e: In 743 816: hundred thousands 7, ten thousands 4, thousands 3, hundreds 8, tens 1, ones 6. The ten thousands digit is 4.

items.q: Which number is forty thousand five hundred three?
items.e: Say the thousands part first: forty thousand → 40. Then write the rest with three digits: five hundred three → 503. So the number is 40 503. 4 503 leaves out the 0 in the thousands place.

items.q: Which number is three hundred six thousand forty?
items.e: Say the thousands part first: three hundred six thousand → 306. Then write the rest with three digits: forty → 040. So the number is 306 040.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. In 750 382 the red 0 is in the thousands place.

items.q: Which number is five hundred twenty thousand seven?
items.e: Say the thousands part first: five hundred twenty thousand → 520. Then write the rest with three digits: seven → 007. So the number is 520 007.

items.q: In 590 264, which digit is in the thousands place?
items.e: In 590 264: hundred thousands 5, ten thousands 9, thousands 0, hundreds 2, tens 6, ones 4. The thousands digit is 0. The 0 shows there are no thousands.

items.q: Which number is eight hundred fifteen thousand four hundred?
items.e: Say the thousands part first: eight hundred fifteen thousand → 815. Then write the rest with three digits: four hundred → 400. So the number is 815 400. Fifteen is 15, not 50.

items.q: A soccer club’s total attendance for the season was two hundred and six thousand and forty. How is this written in digits?
items.e: Two hundred and six thousand → 206. Forty → 040 (no hundreds, so write 0). Fill every empty place with 0: 206 040.

items.q: Three concerts sold 65 407, 65 740, 65 074 tickets. Which list shows these numbers from smallest to greatest?
items.e: All three have 65 thousand. Compare the hundreds: 0 < 4 < 7. Order: 65 074, 65 407, 65 740.

items.q: A theme park had 300 000 visitors by the end of May, 400 000 by the end of June and 500 000 by the end of July. The total goes up by 100 000 each month. By the end of which month will it reach 900 000?
items.e: Count on in 100 000s: August 600 000, September 700 000, October 800 000, November 900 000.

items.q: Johan thinks of a number. It has 4 hundred thousands, 0 ten thousands, 7 thousands, 0 hundreds, 3 tens and 5 ones. What is his number?
items.e: Write the digits in order: 4, 0, 7, 0, 3, 5 → 407 035. The zeros keep every digit in the right place.

items.q: A stadium had 58 900 fans at one match. At the next match there were 10 000 more fans. How many fans were at the next match?
items.e: 10 000 more: only the ten thousands digit changes. 5 ten thousands → 6 ten thousands. 58 900 + 10 000 = 68 900 fans.

items.q: The average distance from the Earth to the Moon is 384 400 km. What is the value of the digit 3?
items.e: The 3 is in the hundred thousands place, so it is worth 300 000 km.

items.q: Anika has the digit cards 0, 4, 7, 2, 9 and 6. She uses each card once to make the smallest 6-digit number she can. What number does she make?
items.e: Put the smallest digits first, but a 6-digit number cannot start with 0. Start with 2, then 0, then 4, 6, 7, 9: 204 679. (024 679 is really 24 679, a 5-digit number.)

items.q: A town had a population of 99 400. Five years later it had grown by 1 000 people. What is the population now?
items.e: 9 thousands + 1 thousand = 10 thousands, so exchange for 1 ten thousand. Then 9 + 1 = 10 ten thousands, so exchange again for 1 hundred thousand. 99 400 + 1 000 = 100 400.

items.q: A school website had 245 000 visits last year. This year it had 100 000 more. How many visits did it have this year?
items.e: 100 000 more: only the hundred thousands digit changes. 2 → 3. 245 000 + 100 000 = 345 000.

items.q: Amahle has the digit cards 0, 4, 7, 2, 9 and 6. She uses each card once to make the smallest 6-digit number she can. What number does she make?
items.e: Put the smallest digits first, but a 6-digit number cannot start with 0. Start with 2, then 0, then 4, 6, 7, 9: 204 679. (024 679 is really 24 679, a 5-digit number.)

items.q: Ruan thinks of a number. It has 4 hundred thousands, 0 ten thousands, 7 thousands, 0 hundreds, 3 tens and 5 ones. What is his number?
items.e: Write the digits in order: 4, 0, 7, 0, 3, 5 → 407 035. The zeros keep every digit in the right place.

items.q: What number is 800 000 + 600 + 4?
items.e: Put each value in its place and write 0 in every empty place. 800 000 + 600 + 4 → 800 604.

items.q: What number is 300 000 + 70 000 + 20?
items.e: Put each value in its place and write 0 in every empty place. 300 000 + 70 000 + 20 → 370 020.

items.q: 600 000 + ☐ + 7 000 + 200 + 5 = 687 205. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 687 205 has 8 in the ten thousands place. That is worth 80 000.

items.q: ☐ + 30 000 + 40 + 2 = 530 042. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 530 042 has 5 in the hundred thousands place. That is worth 500 000.

items.q: What number is 500 000 + 9?
items.e: Put each value in its place and write 0 in every empty place. 500 000 + 9 → 500 009.

items.q: 700 000 + 4 000 + ☐ = 704 009. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 704 009 has 9 in the ones place. That is worth 9.
The parts are not in order. Sort them from the greatest place: 200 000 + 40 000 + 3 000 + 60 + 1 = 243 061. Do not write the digits in the order you see them.

items.q: 100 000 + 50 000 + ☐ + 6 = 150 086. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 150 086 has 8 in the tens place. That is worth 80.
Work out each part: 9 × 100 000 = 900 000, 6 × 1 000 = 6 000, 5 × 10 = 50. Add them: 906 050. Write 0 in every empty place.

items.q: 453 000 = ☐ thousands. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 453 000 = 453 groups of 1 000, so it is 453 thousands. Check: 453 × 1 000 = 453 000.
Work out each part: 7 × 100 000 = 700 000, 2 × 10 = 20, 9 × 1 = 9. Add them: 700 029. Write 0 in every empty place.

items.q: 260 400 = 1 hundred thousand, ☐ ten thousands and 4 hundreds. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 260 400 = 2 hundred thousands, 6 ten thousands and 4 hundreds. Trade 1 hundred thousand for 10 ten thousands: 10 + 6 = 16 ten thousands. Check: 100 000 + 160 000 + 400 = 260 400.

items.q: Write 192 079 in expanded notation.
items.e: Each digit is worth its place value: 100 000 + 90 000 + 2 000 + 70 + 9.
Put each digit in its place: 406 901.

items.q: Write 139 362 in expanded notation.
items.e: Each digit is worth its place value: 100 000 + 30 000 + 9 000 + 300 + 60 + 2.
Put each digit in its place: 369 607.
Put each digit in its place: 768 972.
Put each digit in its place: 230 165.

items.q: Write 941 635 in expanded notation.
items.e: Each digit is worth its place value: 900 000 + 40 000 + 1 000 + 600 + 30 + 5.

items.q: Write 784 306 in expanded notation.
items.e: Each digit is worth its place value: 700 000 + 80 000 + 4 000 + 300 + 6.

items.q: What is 10 000 more than 245 318?
items.e: Only the ten thousands digit changes: 4 → 5. The other digits stay the same. 245 318 + 10 000 = 255 318.

items.q: What is 100 000 less than 708 452?
items.e: Only the hundred thousands digit changes: 7 → 6. The other digits stay the same. 708 452 − 100 000 = 608 452.

items.q: Count in 100s: 46 800, 46 900, 47 000, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 more than the one before. 47 000 + 100 = 47 100. Only the hundreds digit changes.

items.q: Count in 1 000s: 128 500, 129 500, 130 500, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 1 000 more than the one before. 130 500 + 1 000 = 131 500. Only the thousands digit changes.
Each number is 10 000 more than the one before. 57 450 + 10 000 = 67 450. Only the ten thousands digit changes.

items.q: Count in 100 000s: 150 000, 250 000, 350 000, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 000 more than the one before. 350 000 + 100 000 = 450 000. Only the hundred thousands digit changes.
Only the ten thousands digit changes: 3, 4, 5, 6. So each number is 10 000 more than the one before.
Only the thousands digit changes and it gets smaller: 8, 7, 6, 5. So the rule is take away 1 000.

items.q: 10 000 more than a number is 482 150. What is the number?
items.e: Work backwards. If 10 000 more than the number is 482 150, the number is 10 000 less than 482 150: 472 150.

items.q: 100 000 less than a number is 360 400. What is the number?
items.e: Work backwards. If 100 000 less than the number is 360 400, the number is 100 000 more than 360 400: 460 400.

items.q: What is 1 000 more than 39 600?
items.e: 9 thousands + 1 thousand = 10 thousands. Exchange them for 1 ten thousand: the 3 becomes 4 and the thousands digit becomes 0. 39 600 + 1 000 = 40 600.

items.q: What is 100 more than 64 950?
items.e: 9 hundreds + 1 hundred = 10 hundreds. Exchange them for 1 thousand: 4 thousands become 5 and the hundreds digit becomes 0. 64 950 + 100 = 65 050.

items.q: Count in 10s: 5 970, 5 980, 5 990, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more than the one before. 5 990 + 10 = 6 000. 9 tens + 1 ten = 10 tens: exchange them for 1 hundred. Now there are 10 hundreds: exchange them for 1 thousand.

items.q: What is 10 000 less than 503 214?
items.e: There are 0 ten thousands, so exchange 1 hundred thousand for 10 ten thousands. 10 − 1 = 9 ten thousands and 4 hundred thousands are left. 503 214 − 10 000 = 493 214.

items.q: What is 10 000 more than 896 000?
items.e: 9 ten thousands + 1 ten thousand = 10 ten thousands. Exchange them for 1 hundred thousand: 8 becomes 9 and the ten thousands digit becomes 0. 896 000 + 10 000 = 906 000.

items.q: Count backwards in 5s. What number goes in the box? 7 055, 7 050, 7 045, ☐
items.e: Each jump is − 5. The missing number is 7 040.

items.q: Count backwards in 50s. What number goes in the box? 5 050, 5 000, 4 950, ☐
items.e: Each jump is − 50. The missing number is 4 900.

items.q: Count forwards in 2s. What number goes in the box? 7 788, ☐, 7 792, 7 794
items.e: Each jump is + 2. The missing number is 7 790.

items.q: Count forwards in 100s. What number goes in the box? 6 200, ☐, 6 400, 6 500
items.e: Each jump is + 100. The missing number is 6 300.

items.q: Count forwards in 50s. What number goes in the box? 7 250, 7 300, ☐, 7 400
items.e: Each jump is + 50. The missing number is 7 350.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 7 hundreds is more than 6 hundreds. So 45 762 > 45 672.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 300 000 to 400 000 there are 10 equal jumps, so each mark is 10 000, not 1 000. The arrow is 6 marks after 300 000: 300 000 + 60 000 = 360 000.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the ten thousands place: 7 ten thousands is more than 4 ten thousands. So 874 321 > 847 123. 874 321 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the thousands place: 9 thousands is more than 3 thousands. So 829 435 > 823 945. 823 945 is the smallest.

items.q: Which number is between 450 000 and 460 000?
items.e: Numbers between 450 000 and 460 000 have 4 hundred thousands and 5 ten thousands. 455 800 fits. 45 980 has only 5 digits, so it is much smaller.

items.q: Put 786 324, 738 624, 763 824 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 738 624 < 763 824 (ten thousands: 3 < 6). 763 824 < 786 324 (ten thousands: 6 < 8). So the order is 738 624, 763 824, 786 324.

items.q: Put 172 358, 123 758, 135 728 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 123 758 < 135 728 (ten thousands: 2 < 3). 135 728 < 172 358 (ten thousands: 3 < 7). So the order is 123 758, 135 728, 172 358.

items.q: Put 635 287, 623 587, 652 387 in order from greatest to smallest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 623 587 < 635 287 (ten thousands: 2 < 3). 635 287 < 652 387 (ten thousands: 3 < 5). So the order is 652 387, 635 287, 623 587.

items.q: 6☐4 500 > 674 000. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The hundred thousands are the same (6). Compare the ten thousands: the box must be 7 or more. 4, 5 and 6 are too small. 684 500 > 674 000.

items.q: 3☐,850 < 34 100. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The ten thousands are the same (3). Compare the thousands: the box must be 4 or less. If it is 4, compare the hundreds: 8 > 1, so 34 850 would be too big. 33 850 < 34 100.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: 89 999 has only 5 digits, so it is the least, even though it starts with 8. Every 6-digit number is at least 100 000.

items.q: Put 453 000, 435 000, 450 300 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: All have 4 hundred thousands. Ten thousands: 3 < 5, so 435 000 is the least. 453 000 and 450 300 both have 5 ten thousands. Thousands: 0 < 3, so 450 300 < 453 000. Order: 435 000, 450 300, 453 000.

items.q: Use each of the digits 7, 2, 9, 4, 1 and 6 once. What is the greatest number you can make?
items.e: Put the biggest digit in the hundred thousands place, then the next biggest, and so on: 9, 7, 6, 4, 2, 1. The greatest number is 976 421.

items.q: Put 612 040, 164 020, 621 040 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: Hundred thousands: 1 < 6, so 164 020 is the least. 612 040 and 621 040 both have 6 hundred thousands. Ten thousands: 2 > 1, so 621 040 > 612 040. Order: 621 040, 612 040, 164 020.

items.q: Which number is between 799 000 and 801 000?
items.e: 800 150 is more than 800 000 and less than 801 000, so it is between 799 000 and 801 000. 801 500 is too big, 790 900 is too small and 80 015 has only 5 digits.

items.q: Use each of the digits 5, 0, 8, 3, 6 and 1 once. What is the least 6-digit number you can make?
items.e: A 6-digit number cannot start with 0. Put the smallest other digit first: 1. Then 0, 3, 5, 6, 8: 103 568. (013 568 is just 13 568, which has only 5 digits.)

items.q: Put 99 500, 105 000, 100 500, 95 050 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: The 5-digit numbers are less than the 6-digit numbers. 95 050 < 99 500 (thousands: 5 < 9). 100 500 < 105 000 (thousands: 0 < 5). Order: 95 050, 99 500, 100 500, 105 000.

items.q: 38☐ 400 > 386 500. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The hundred thousands and ten thousands are the same. Compare the thousands: the box must be 6 or more. If it is 6, compare the hundreds: 4 < 5, so 386 400 is too small. 388 400 > 386 500.

items.q: Use each of the digits 6, 0, 2, 0, 9 and 5 once. What is the greatest number you can make?
items.e: Biggest digit first: 9, then 6, then 5, then 2. The two 0s go last, in the tens and ones places: 965 200.

items.q: 625 ☐80 < 625 450. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The first three digits are the same. Compare the hundreds: the box must be 4 or less. If it is 4, compare the tens: 8 > 5, so 625 480 is too big. 625 380 < 625 450.
